what: Diagnosis of sv-memory project vs Graphify competitor
why: User asked to verify the project idea (memory + knowledge graph for AI agents, token reduction) and benchmark against github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify. Project exploration confirmed all README claims are implemented (SQLite+FTS5, Leiden, betweenness, god nodes, 25 MCP tools, chunked Git sync, protocol injection). Key discrepancies noted: go 1.22+ vs actual 1.26.3, README says memories.json but code uses chunks/, mcp.go comment says 19 tools (actually 25), no tests in cmd/. Graphify has 96.6k stars, YC S26, ~40 languages, EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS edge tags, HTTP MCP transport, PDF/media support, 8 LLM backends, 20+ platforms, published benchmarks.
learned: sv-memory's unique value vs Graphify = combining persistent architectural decision memory (mem0-style) with structural code graph. Graphify is pure graph; mem0/supermemory are pure memory. The differentiation must be preserved and defended. Confidence tags (EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS), benchmarks, HTTP MCP transport, strict-mode hooks, and .sv-memory-ignore are the highest-priority gaps to close. Avoid pdf/media/many-LLM-backends (they dilute the local-first identity).
author: Mario Sandoval (Sv Tech)
next_steps: 1) Fix 3 README discrepancies (Go version, chunks sync, 25 tools count). 2) Add EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS edge confidence tags in internal/graph/extractor/. 3) Add benchmarks validating token savings. 4) Add HTTP MCP transport. 5) Add strict mode for source reads. 6) Add .sv-memory-ignore. 7) Write tests for cmd/sv-memory/. 8) Remove stray root binary.
